title: Who is Maria? Identity resolution
objective: Learners see how the strictness of match rules decides whether a health plan gets one correct profile per member, wrongly merges two different people, or leaves duplicates.

recommended.why: An animated story follows each record from its source system into a profile, so learners see exactly which link pulled a stranger in and which record was left behind.

alternative.why: Following the records versus seeing the match graph: which makes the false-merge risk obvious?

assumptions: People, records, emails, phones and addresses are fictional
Matching is simplified: one deterministic rule at a time, no scoring, no survivorship or data quality steps
Fuzzy name = lower case, nickname map (Mia to Maria), then optimal string alignment edit distance; names match when similarity is at least 85 %
Records that match are linked transitively (union-find): if A matches B and B matches C, all three form one profile
Maria Lopez and Mario Lopez share a home phone and address; Maria Lopes and Mario Lopez share a date of birth
A false merge is a profile that mixes records of different people; a duplicate is each extra profile one person is split across
checkDescription: Profiles are exactly the connected components of the matching pairs, every record sits in exactly one profile, correct profiles, false merges and duplicates are recounted from the ground truth, and the default rule gives 3 correct profiles with none of either error.

learnerPrompts.predict: Before you switch to "Email or phone": which two people do you expect to end up in one profile, and why?
learnerPrompts.explain: With "Fuzzy name only", Maria Lopes never directly matches Mario Lopez, yet they share a profile. Why, and what could Mario now see?
